Write a data frame to csv, named after the variable that was passed in

Source: R/io-export.R
write.csv_rawr.Rd

Looks up the name input was called with (via deparse(substitute())) and writes it to <folder>/<prefix>_<name>.csv (or <folder>/<name>.csv when prefix is NULL) — an intentional NSE pattern that lets ~30 export call sites stay terse (write.csv_rawr(counts_pep_all_condition)) while the output filename always matches the object name.

Usage

write.csv_rawr(input, folder, prefix = NULL)

Arguments

input

The data frame to write (NSE: its variable name becomes the filename).

folder

Destination directory for the csv.

prefix

Optional string prepended to the filename as "<prefix>_<name>.csv"; when NULL (the default) the filename is just "<name>.csv".

Value

Invisible NULL; called for its side effect of writing a csv.

Details

Reconciles three near-duplicate report-inline variants (a plain folder = FolderResults-defaulting version, and two that additionally prefixed the filename with params$Subset) into one canonical signature that takes both folder and an optional prefix explicitly.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
write.csv_rawr(counts_pep_all_condition, folder = FolderResults)
write.csv_rawr(counts_pep_all_wide, folder = FolderResults, prefix = params$Subset)
} # }
